mainEntity.name: What does chenille mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chenille is French for caterpillar, after the fuzzy, raised yarn texture.

mainEntity.name: How are chenille patches made?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yarn is looped in layers onto a felt base, with short lengths caught between longer strands to build the raised pile.

mainEntity.name: Are they iron-on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Iron-on chenille lasts 50+ washes when applied with a heat press at 285°F. For heavy letterman jackets, sew-on is the most permanent.

mainEntity.name: Can I wash chenille patches?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Wash cold, inside out, with mild detergent. Our patches hold up through 100 test washes without fraying.

mainEntity.name: Why does chenille cost more than embroidery?

acceptedAnswer.text: It needs dedicated chenille machines and more material per patch. In return it has the premium look buyers associate with varsity gear.

mainEntity.name: Chenille or embroidered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chenille suits bold, simple shapes with large fill areas. Embroidery suits fine detail and small text. Many letters combine both.

mainEntity.name: Can I mix backings in one order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Note the split on your quote request.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between embroidered and woven patches?

acceptedAnswer.text: Embroidered patches are stitched onto a fabric base, which gives raised texture. Woven patches are made by interlacing fine threads on a loom, which gives a flatter patch that holds smaller text and finer detail.

mainEntity.name: How long does an embroidered patch order take?

mainEntity.name: How long do embroidered patches last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two to three years of regular wear and washing is normal, and much longer with cold washes and air drying.

mainEntity.name: What sizes work best?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cap fronts take 2.25–2.5 in, left chest 4–5 in, across the chest 10–12 in and jacket backs 12–14 in. Any custom size is possible.

mainEntity.name: What is a PVC patch?

acceptedAnswer.text: A patch molded from soft polyvinyl chloride. It is waterproof, flexible and reproduces fine lines and small text that thread cannot hold at small sizes.

mainEntity.name: Are PVC patches waterproof and washable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They do not absorb water and can go through the washing machine. Wash cold and inside out if the patch is attached with adhesive.

mainEntity.name: Will they fade in the Arizona sun?

acceptedAnswer.text: PVC is UV-resistant and the color runs through each layer, so it does not fade, fray, crack or peel under normal outdoor use.

mainEntity.name: Can I iron on a PVC patch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not with a household iron directly on the patch. Use hook-and-loop, sew-on or adhesive backing, or a heat press with fabric adhesive at 160°C / 320°F for 20–30 seconds.

mainEntity.name: How thick are they?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard patches are about 2 mm, with raised design elements around 0.7 mm. We also make 3 mm patches for tactical and heavy-fabric use.

mainEntity.name: Is there a mold fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Tooling is included in the patch price, and reorders of the same design get 25% off per piece.

mainEntity.name: Can I get a physical sample before a big order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every order gets a free digital proof, and large orders can get a pre-production sample; the cost depends on order size.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between 2D and 3D PVC?

acceptedAnswer.text: 2D has flat layers and costs less. 3D adds sculpted depth for a premium feel.

mainEntity.name: What are silicone labels?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raised, rubber-like labels made from silicone polymer that tolerate hot and cold temperatures.

mainEntity.name: How are they attached?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a heat press. The self-adhesive backing bonds at 160°C / 320°F in about 15 seconds.

mainEntity.name: Are they safe on clothing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They are soft and gentle against skin.

mainEntity.name: Are they waterproof?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, they handle sweat and rain well. Long submersion or a poorly sealed edge can let water under, so press firmly.

mainEntity.name: Are they better for the environment than PVC?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are not fully biodegradable, but silicone is generally considered a better choice than PVC, lasts a long time and is recyclable.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Silicone labels start from $2.50 per piece. Send the label size, quantity and artwork through the quote form and we will reply with your exact per-piece price.

mainEntity.name: How are woven patches made?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a jacquard loom that interlaces polyester or cotton threads into the design, instead of stitching thread onto a base.

mainEntity.name: Are woven patches good for small designs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The finer thread keeps small text and thin details readable.

mainEntity.name: Woven or embroidered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Woven is thinner, sleeker and holds more detail. Embroidered is thicker, more textured and generally the more rugged of the two.

mainEntity.name: Can I wash them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Wash the garment gently; hand washing keeps woven patches looking new the longest.

mainEntity.name: Which backing do you recommend?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sew-on for the strongest hold, or iron-on with paper backing for a clean feel on light garments.

mainEntity.name: Why is payment taken upfront?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every order is made to your design and cannot be resold, so production starts once the order is paid and the proof is approved.

home.title: Custom Patches Arizona | Embroidered, PVC & Chenille Patches
home.description: Custom embroidered, PVC, chenille, woven, printed and leather patches for Arizona. 5-piece minimum, free design and digital proof, 7–14 business days delivered, free tracked shipping anywhere in Arizona.

mainEntity.name: What types of custom patches do you make?

acceptedAnswer.text: Embroidered, PVC, chenille, woven, printed (sublimated), leather, sequin, silicone labels and hook-and-loop patches, plus keychains and PVC shoe charms.

mainEntity.name: How do I apply an iron-on patch?

acceptedAnswer.text: A heat press gives the strongest bond: 160°C / 320°F for 15–20 seconds for most patches, then let it cool. With a household iron, set it for your fabric, cover the patch with a thin cloth and press firmly for 20–30 seconds. See the iron-on guide for each patch type.

mainEntity.name: Can I wash clothes with patches on them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Wash inside out in cold water and air dry. Embroidered and PVC patches handle about 50 washes this way; sewn-on patches last the longest.

mainEntity.name: Can patches be removed later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sew-on patches come off by cutting the stitches. Iron-on patches can be loosened with heat and peeled, though some adhesive may remain. Velcro patches simply pull off.

mainEntity.name: Is there a minimum order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patches start at 5 pieces. A few products have their own minimums, like 50 keychains or 100 shoe charms per design. The per-piece price drops as quantity goes up.

mainEntity.name: What sizes and shapes can I order?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any shape. Common sizes are 2.25–2.5 in for caps, 4–5 in for the left chest, 10–12 in across the chest and 12–14 in for jacket backs.

mainEntity.name: Do you make patches for hats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Hat patches are sized to curve with the crown, in embroidery, leather, PVC or woven, with iron-on, sew-on or Velcro backing.

mainEntity.name: How long does an order take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most orders arrive 7–14 business days after you approve the proof. Rush production is available; tell us your date before you order so we can confirm it.

mainEntity.name: Do I see a proof first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Always. Every order gets a free digital proof with unlimited revisions, and nothing is produced until you approve it.

mainEntity.name: Which backing should I choose?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sew-on for the most permanent hold, iron-on for quick near-permanent application, Velcro for patches you swap, and peel-and-stick for one-day use.

mainEntity.name: Do you take wholesale and resale orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Brands, decorators and distributors get monthly volume pricing, designs kept on file and white-label packaging.

mainEntity.name: Who orders custom patches in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: Work crews and service companies, fire and EMS departments, schools and booster clubs, sports teams, riding clubs, hat and apparel brands, breweries and restaurants, scouts, and families.

mainEntity.name: Will my bulk order look consistent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Approved files and thread colors are kept on file and every run is inspected against the approved proof, so patch 5,000 matches patch 1.

mainEntity.name: Do you ship everywhere in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Shipping is free and tracked to any Arizona address, from Phoenix and Tucson to Flagstaff, Yuma and small towns in between.
